newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S MADUNA WANTS TO FACE PARLY ON OIL SCAM.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S MADUNA WANTS TO FACE PARLY ON OIL SCAM.

text.p: South African Minerals and Energy Minister Penuell Maduna said on Wednesday that he wanted to appear before parliamentarians to rebut charges he wrongly accused the Central Energy Fund (CEF) of malpractice.
"It's my intention to deal with the matter within the structures of parliament," Maduna told a press briefing. "I want to appear in front of the public accounts committee."

South Africa's Auditor General Henri Kluever on Monday cleared the CEF and its general manager of any error or malpractice concerning an alleged 170 million rand loss from the country's strategic oil stock.
"This amount does not represent a loss or theft of oil or a transfer of oil to any other person, it is simply an accounting entry," Deputy Auditor General Bertie Loots told reporters.

The auditor general, parliament's watchdog on public spending, engaged auditors Price Waterhouse Meyer Nel to examine the CEF's accounts after Maduna publicly accused the auditor's office earlier this year of "some nimble footwork" to cover the alleged loss.
Maduna subsequently suspended CEF general manager Kobus van Zyl on full pay pending the outcome of an investigation he ordered by an independent Cape Town-based auditor.
The CEF was set up under apartheid to manage South Africa's oil purchases and stocks in the face of international sanctions imposed in 1977 and lifted in 1994.

Maduna said on Wednesday that the speaker of parliament was trying to arrange a time for him to appear in front of the parliamentary public accounts committee, but chairman Ken Andrew said he had not yet been contacted about this.
The minister said that, at the time he had good grounds to be worried about an apparent loss and he questioned the way the figures had been presented to parliament.
